Install over your current version, or let the app update itself. Your projects, databases and settings are kept. After updating, restart MySQL and MariaDB once so they pick up the new listening addresses.
- `php artisan serve` (and any PHP started by PHP) now loads LampRabit's `php.ini`, fixing "could not find driver" for MySQL and MariaDB.
- MySQL and MariaDB also listen on `::1`, so clients set to `localhost` connect every time (Windows resolves `localhost` to `::1` first).
- **Overview** shows framework

Apache, Nginx, PHP, Redis and Memcached for Linux and macOS, and Memcached for Windows (nono303's Cygwin build, https://github.com/nono303/memcached), downloaded by lampRabit's Services page. Built by .github/workflows/binaries.yml from build/linux/; checksums are in manifest.json. Sources: https://github.com/redis/redis, https://github.com/memcached/memcached, Cygwin https://cygwin.com/

- **New projects** won't quietly reuse an existing database (a Laravel project would otherwise run its migrations there), and MariaDB's own system databases can't be chosen. Reserved Windows names like `CON` are refused.

A small follow-up to 0.1.0 that tidies up the project for its public launch. If you already have lampRabit 0.1.0, it will offer this update by itself; click **Install** and it restarts on the new version.

## What's new

- **License:** lampRabit is now officially open source under the **MIT License**.
- **Easier to report problems:** new bug-report and feature-request forms on GitHub. Attach the diagnostics report from **Settings → Troubleshooting → Run diagnostics → Copy**.
- **Clearer installation g

The first public release of **lampRabit**: a local PHP development environment. **Windows is fully supported; macOS and Linux builds are a preview** (see below). Start Apache or Nginx, PHP and MariaDB with one click, and every folder in `www` becomes a site at `https://<folder>.test`.
- **New projects:** blank, static, Laravel, Symfony or WordPress, optionally with a database.
The app runs on macOS and Linux, but **Apache, Nginx and PHP can't be downloaded there yet**, so you can't serve PHP sites with it o
SQLite Lens is now **Omasql**, with a new icon that sits beside Omacut, Omawrite, and Omacalc. History, recent files, and drafts move over from the old name on first start.
Lode is now **SQLite Lens**. History, recent files, and drafts move over from `~/.local/state/lode` on first start.

First release: SQL editor with highlighting and completion, schema browser, sortable results grid, row inspector with JSON formatting, history, CSV export, and confirmation before destructive statements. Follows the Omarchy theme and language live.
